domains.Number Theory / Valuation Theory: Ostrowski's theorem (1916), p-adic valuations, adele ring, product formula — the claim is that frequency IS a valuation-theoretic object, not an Archimedean real number.
domains.Physics / Quantum Foundations: Compton frequency ν_C = mc²/h is the particle's invariant identity. In Planck units, it's a dimensionless rational. The claim dissolves particle 'thingness' into recurring distinction-patterns. Every fundamental particle IS its prime spectrum.
domains.Condensed Matter Physics: Quasiparticle frequencies depend on environmental parameters (lattice spacing, temperature), not universal rationals. This operationalizes the fundamental/quasi distinction: fundamental = universal rational invariant; quasi = environmental rational.
domains.Information Theory / Computer Science: Frequency = count per time = bits per step. In discrete time (Planck steps), frequency is an information-theoretic rate. The Bekenstein bound relates information to area in dimensionless Planck units. Radix trees / tries encode the valuation-theoretic structure — the Bruhat-Tits tree IS a radix tree over the primes.
domains.Mathematics / Category Theory: The adelic frequency framework dissolves the distinction between mathematical structure and physical reality. The adele ring and idele class group are the natural objects; the Archimedean continuum is ONE projection. Category theory provides the invariant-pattern language: the universe is a dagger compact category with adelic structure.

isomorphisms.Number Theory \u2192 Physics: The p-adic valuation ord_p(q) of a rational frequency IS the depth coordinate on the Bruhat-Tits tree. The tree's boundary IS the p-adic projective line P^1(Q_p). This is not an analogy — the frequency as rational number literally lives in the tree.
isomorphisms.Physics \u2192 Condensed Matter: A quasiparticle's frequency is an environmental rational (ratio of material parameters) vs. a fundamental particle's frequency is a universal rational (Compton count). The prime spectrum distinguishes them: fundamental particles have fixed valuations at ALL primes; quasiparticles lack p-adic invariance.
isomorphisms.Physics \u2192 Information Theory: Frequency = cycles / Planck times = the information rate of a periodic process. The Bekenstein bound I ≤ 2πRE/(h c ln 2) → I ≤ 2πRE/ln 2 in dimensionless Planck units. R and E are themselves rational ratios (length in Planck lengths, energy in Planck energies). The entire bound is a statement about integer counts on a radix tree.
isomorphisms.Information Theory \u2192 Number Theory: A radix tree over base p IS the Bruhat-Tits tree T_p. Each node at level k represents a p-adic ball of radius p^{-k}. The tree encodes exactly the p-adic ultrametric that makes frequencies into valuation-theoretic objects. Fredkin's trie (1960) = Serre's tree (1980) — same structure, different language.
isomorphisms.Category Theory \u2192 Physics: The adele ring A and idele class group C_K are not models of physics — they are the canonical mathematical objects on which harmonic analysis (Tate's thesis) yields the Riemann zeta function. If physics IS the study of the unique self-consistent invariant pattern, and that pattern is the adelic one, then 'physics' and 'adelic number theory' are the same conversation in different rooms.

meta_principle: Across ALL domains, the invariant is: a rational ratio a/b ∈ Q, carrying valuations at every place, determines a hierarchical (tree-structured) coordinate, where the levels correspond to prime powers and the cross-ratios between nodes determine the physical observables. The Archimedean projection (real numbers) is ONE branch of the full valuation-theoretic structure.
